display.purpose: Page titles ("Finanzas", "Agenda") and the kiosk's event-name hero.

label.purpose: Form field labels, metadata lines, status badges.

mono.purpose: Literal identifiers only — event slugs, filesystem watch paths.

shadows.name: photo-lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow role in the system — applied exclusively under a rendered photo (kiosk hero, guest photo, wall/lightbox images) so it reads as a physical object over a flat room.

shadows.name: photo-lift-deep
shadows.purpose: Slightly heavier variant of photo-lift used on the kiosk's hero photo.

motion.name: press-feedback
motion.purpose: Universal tap/press feedback on every button and interactive tile.

motion.name: photo-drop-in
motion.purpose: Polaroid drop-in entrance for wall photo tiles — falls in tilted, overshoots, settles flat. Staggered per tile via --photo-delay.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default hover/focus color and opacity transitions.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The system's one high-intent action — submit, share, "+ Nueva reserva". Flash Magenta Deep (not the brighter Flash Magenta — that shade fails AA contrast with white text at this size), always a pill.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #db2777; color: #ffffff; font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 9999px; border: none; transition: background 0.15s ease-out, transform 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ec4899; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.95); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.3; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Every non-primary action and the top-of-page navigation pills ("Eventos", "Agenda", "Cancelar").
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.10); color: rgba(255,255,255,0.70); font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 9999px; border: none; transition: background 0.15s ease-out, transform 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.16); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.95); }

components.name: Download Button
components.description: Signature variant: styled as a physical print leaving the system, not as UI — Paper White fill, void-black text. Reserved for the guest's "Descargar" action.
components.css: .ds-btn-download { background: #ffffff; color: #18181b; font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; padding: 12px 24px; border-radius: 9999px; border: none; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; transition: transform 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-download:active { transform: scale(0.95); }

components.name: Status Badge — Active
components.description: Confirmed/active state — event is live, agenda entry confirmed. Same Flash Magenta Deep fill and AA-contrast reasoning as the primary button.
components.css: .ds-badge-active { display: inline-block; background: #db2777; color: #ffffff; font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.75rem; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 9999px; }

components.name: Status Badge — Inactive
components.description: Pending/inactive state — same shape as Active, quieter fill.
components.css: .ds-badge-inactive { display: inline-block; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.10); color: rgba(255,255,255,0.50); font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.75rem; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 9999px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The default frosted-panel container for every list item, form, and dashboard section. Flat — no shadow, no border.
components.css: .ds-card { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.10); border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; } .ds-card-title { font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.90); margin: 0 0 4px; } .ds-card-body { font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.25rem; color: #34d399; margin: 0; }

components.name: Input
components.description: Frosted-panel text field, no resting border — the focus ring is the only border-like treatment in the system.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; } .ds-field-label { font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.70); } .ds-input { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.10); color: #ffffff; font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; outline: none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.30); } .ds-input:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #ec4899; }

narrative.overview:
Pix lives in the moment right after the flash — a dark room lit by one bright thing at a time. The canvas is void-black (#18181b), the same tone as the venue itself: no card is whiter than it needs to be, no section fights the photo for attention. Against that dark field, exactly one accent gets to be loud — magenta (flash magenta on the canvas itself, its deeper shade under white text on a filled surface) — used the way a strobe is used: rare, sudden, and always on something that matters (a primary action, an active state, a confirmed status). Everything else is frosted glass: translucent white-on-black panels (bg-white/10) that read as UI chrome without ever competing with what's printed on the "paper" above them.

The system is unapologetically tactile — full pill buttons, saturated fills, visible press feedback (active:scale-95) — built for a phone tapped once in a dark room, not a mouse hovering a desktop. Depth is rationed on purpose: everywhere that isn't a photograph is flat, tonal layering only; the one place shadows and blur are allowed to exist is around an actual photo, which is the system's only "object" — everything else is surface. Iconography leans on real emoji instead of a drawn icon set, which keeps the voice playful and instantly legible in Spanish-first copy without adding an icon library.

This is one visual language, not two: the guest-facing kiosk/wall/photo pages and the operator's Spanish-language admin screens (agenda, finance, inventory) share the exact same tokens, components, and rules. The admin side is not a "serious business" reskin — it's the same neon-instant room, just with tables and forms instead of a QR code.
keyCharacteristics: Void-black canvas, one magenta accent used sparingly and only for what matters most
Frosted-glass panels (white/10) — flat, tonal, no shadows on UI chrome
Full-pill buttons and badges; rounded-lg for containers; a dedicated, more generous radius reserved only for photographic imagery
Depth (shadow, blur) exists only around real photos and the full-screen lightbox — a physical object in a flat room
Tactile press feedback (active:scale-95/98) on every tappable element
Emoji as the icon system, throughout guest and admin surfaces alike

rules.name: The One Strobe Rule
rules.body: Flash Magenta lights up exactly one thing at a time — the primary action or the confirmed state — never a background, a large panel, or more than one competing element in the same view. Its rarity is what makes it read as "on."

rules.name: The Paper Exception Rule
rules.body: Paper White is reserved for things meant to feel like a physical print leaving the system — the QR code and the "Descargar" button. Nothing else gets a white surface.

rules.name: The Deep-Fill Rule
rules.body: White text sits only on Flash Magenta Deep, never on the brighter Flash Magenta — the bright shade drops below WCAG AA (3.5:1) under white text at button/badge size. The bright shade is for color-on-black uses only (rings, links, thin decorative fills).

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one font family in this system. A new surface never introduces a second typeface for "contrast" — hierarchy comes from weight, size, and opacity only.

rules.name: The Flat Room Rule
rules.body: UI chrome never casts a shadow. If something needs to look lifted off the page, it is a photograph (or the overlay holding one) — not a button, card, or panel.

dos: Do ration Flash Magenta to one element per screen — the primary action or the single active state. If two things on screen are magenta, one of them is wrong.
Do use rounded-full for anything tappable and rounded-lg for anything that just contains content — never mix the two roles.
Do reserve rounded-photo and shadow-2xl exclusively for actual photographic imagery.
Do use the four white-opacity text steps (/90, /70, /50, /30) as the entire neutral text scale — don't introduce a gray hex value.
Do give every tappable element active:scale-95-style press feedback.
Do reach for an emoji before reaching for an SVG icon; it's the established icon system.
Do give every icon-only button (no visible text label, e.g. a bare 🗑️) an explicit aria-label — an emoji is not announced as its meaning by assistive tech.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow to a card, button, badge, or input — depth belongs to photographs only.
Don't introduce a second accent color; Neon Emerald and Warning Coral are semantic (money in/out) only, never decorative.
Don't add a border/stroke to a resting input or card — separation comes from opacity and radius, not lines.
Don't build a visually distinct "admin theme" — agenda/finance/inventory use the exact same tokens and components as the guest-facing kiosk/wall/guest pages.
Don't introduce a second font family for hierarchy or "personality" — Poppins carries the whole system at every weight and size.
